series: Jev & The Next Generation of AI Automation
title: AI guardrails and tool safety
subtitle: Put allow / deny / escalate in front of shell, deploy, delete and data-mutating tools — and measure false negatives like production incidents.

takeaways: Tool safety is a decision problem, not a prose refusal problem.
Optimise for false negatives on irreversible actions.
Never test destructive gates against production.

body.text: Why this matters

Coding harnesses learned the hard way that agents will cheerfully run dangerous commands when persuaded. LangChain’s Auto Mode narrative argues that cheap classifiers make the same pattern available to every agent runtime.
Reference policy

items: Classify tool name + args + recent trace.
Deny on high risk; escalate on medium/uncertain; allow on low.
Log evidence for later training and audit.

body.text: Benchmark C methodology

TenthMatrix’s suite uses synthetic tool calls spanning read_file, write_file, shell, git, deploy, delete, database and network. Labels are reviewed. Metrics: detection rate, false positives, false negatives, latency, cost. Destructive calls execute only in ephemeral sandboxes — never against shared prod.
What we know / don’t
We know policy middleware is shipping in multiple ecosystems. We do not know a universal risk taxonomy — your deny list is product-specific.

Conclusion
If an action can delete customer data, the gate must fail closed. Speed matters, but false negatives matter more.
